stories.headline: J&K BJP distances itself from slogans, ‘berating Kashmir women’, during rally in Kashmir
stories.deck: Ruling National Conference said the apology tendered by the BJP spokesman “was not enough”
stories.bodyText:
Facing public outcry, the BJP on Thursday (August 6, 2025) distanced itself from the slogans, which allegedly berated women of Kashmir, raised during a celebratory rally held in south Kashmir’s Anantnag on the seventh anniversary of abrogation of Article 370 on August 5.
“The slogans allegedly raised by some individuals should not be attributed to the BJP as an organisation. The party does not endorse any defamatory or derogatory remarks against anyone. The party will take action against such individuals,” said BJP spokesman Altaf Thakur.
The BJP statement came a day after the party activists allegedly raised slogans, referring to popular women names Aazi and Fazi in Kashmir. “Moukloy Aazi hund te Faazi hund izzat [Honour of Aazi and Fazi has ended],” said the slogans, in a procession taken out by senior BJP leader Sofi Yousuf.
“The party has always upheld the dignity and honour of women and that the 33% reservation for women reflects its commitment to women’s empowerment. The BJP remains committed to political decorum, issue-based politics and strengthening the participation of women in public life,” said Mr. Thakur.
He said the party’s policies and public conduct are guided by the principles of respect, democracy and constitutional values.
Ruling National Conference said the apology tendered by the BJP spokesman “was not enough”. “Aazi and Fazi are not just names; they are our mothers, our sisters, our identity. Mocking them was an insult to every Kashmiri and to our culture. Leader of Opposition Sunil Sharma should tender a public apology,” said NC leader and legislator Tanvir Sadiq.
He said some insults were not directed at individuals but “at an entire society”.

stories.headline: NHRC sends notice to Madhya Pradesh govt over assault on Dalit student by teacher
US court slaps Meta with $567 million penalty in landmark child safety ruling
stories.bodyText:
A New Mexico state court has ordered Meta to pay $567 million and overhaul safety features for young users after finding the social media company responsible for harming children's mental health. The ruling marks one of the largest legal actions against a social media platform over child safety and is expected to influence similar lawsuits across the United States.
Judge Bryan Biedscheid ruled that Meta had created a public nuisance in New Mexico, siding with Attorney General Raúl Torrez, who accused the company of designing Facebook and Instagram to keep young users addicted while failing to protect children from sexual exploitation. The court directed Meta to implement a series of youth safety measures for the next five years, including monthly usage limits for teenagers, restrictions on notifications, tighter controls on adult contact with minors, safeguards for AI chatbots and enhanced review of child sexual abuse reports.
The financial penalty will fund programmes aimed at addressing the impact of social media on children. According to the court, $420 million will be allocated to treatment services for young people, while the remaining amount will support awareness campaigns, prevention initiatives, screening services and other related costs over the next five years.
Meta said it would appeal the ruling, maintaining that it has continued to strengthen protections for young users and remove harmful content from its platforms.
"We remain confident in our record of protecting teens online and will continue to defend ourselves against claims that misrepresent the facts," Meta said in a statement.
The ruling follows the first phase of New Mexico's lawsuit, in which a jury in March found that Meta violated the state's consumer protection law by misrepresenting the safety of Facebook and Instagram for young users. Jurors had imposed $375 million in civil penalties, concluding that the company knowingly harmed children's mental health and concealed what it knew about child sexual exploitation on its platforms.
The second phase of the trial, heard without a jury over three weeks, focused on whether Meta's platforms constituted a public nuisance under New Mexico law. Prosecutors sought sweeping changes to the company's products, including curbing addictive features, improving age verification and strengthening default privacy settings to better protect children.
However, the court declined to require mandatory age verification for children under 13, noting that the federal Children's Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA) prevents platforms from collecting additional personal information or passively tracking children for that purpose. The judge also said imposing such a requirement only on Meta, and not on other social media companies, would be "inequitable and unduly injurious" to the company.
The case is being closely watched as states, municipalities and school districts across the United States pursue similar lawsuits seeking industry-wide changes to how social media platforms protect children online.

stories.headline: Rain threat looms large over IND vs SL three-day warm-up match
stories.deck: India's preparations for the two-Test series against Sri Lanka could be affected by rain, with wet weather forecast in Colombo during the three-day warm-up match against Sri Lanka XI. Heavy showers are expected from Friday morning to Sunday afternoon, raising doubts over how much playing time both teams will get before the first Test in Galle.
stories.bodyText:
India will take on Sri Lanka XI in a three-day warm-up match at the Nondescripts Cricket Club Ground in Colombo from Friday. However, the weather forecast does not look encouraging.
According to the forecast, rain, including heavy showers, is expected to affect the city from Friday morning until Sunday afternoon. This could reduce the amount of play and affect India's preparations ahead of the first Test.
India vs Sri Lanka warm-up: Weather report
There is a 90 per cent chance of rain on Friday morning, with around 9.4 mm of rainfall expected. The temperature is likely to be around 30°C, while humidity could touch 78 per cent. Cloud cover is expected to remain at 99 per cent, with visibility reduced to around 5 km.
The weather is not expected to improve much in the afternoon.
The chance of rain remains 70 per cent, with another 4.9 mm of rainfall forecast. The temperature is expected to stay around 29°C, with strong winds and thick cloud cover continuing.
Important match before Test series
The warm-up match is an important part of India's preparations for the two-Test series against Sri Lanka, which begins in Galle on August 15.
Indian batters will use the game to prepare for Sri Lanka's spin attack. 
Spin troubled India in recent home Test series against New Zealand and South Africa, and the team will be eager to adjust to Sri Lankan conditions.
Captain Shubman Gill, KL Rahul and Yashasvi Jaiswal have already practised against spin before travelling to Colombo. However, batting on Sri Lankan pitches in match conditions will provide a better test.
Chance for bowlers to adjust
India's bowling attack will also look to get used to local conditions. With Jasprit Bumrah unavailable because of injury, Mohammed Siraj will lead the pace attack. He will be supported by Prasidh Krishna, Gurnoor Brar, Manav Suthar and Saransh Jain.
Brar and Jain impressed while playing for India A against Sri Lanka A in Galle last month and will be hoping for more valuable time in the middle.
Gambhir wants team to be ready
Head coach Gautam Gambhir urged the players to make full use of the preparation time.
"We know what is in front of us. We can do volume, we can push our limits, we can tick all the boxes and come 15th morning whether we are batting first or bowling first we will be absolutely ready with every answer to every question thrown at us.
"So make sure to tick all the boxes from now on."
The biggest challenge for India, however, could be the weather. If the forecast proves accurate, rain may deny the visitors valuable practice before the opening Test.

stories.headline: Karnataka postpones Agriculture Officers’ recruitment exam after student protests
stories.deck: The Karnataka government on Thursday issued an order revoking the recruitment notification for 128 AO posts and 817 AAO posts.
stories.bodyText:
The Karnataka government has postponed the recruitment examination for Agricultural Officers (AOs) and Assistant Agricultural Officers (AAOs) following the protests by students.
The Karnataka government on Thursday (August 6) issued an order revoking the recruitment notification for 128 AO posts and 817 AAO posts. The order came after agriculture students intensified their protest against the inclusion of graduates from other courses in the eligibility criteria for the examination.
On August 4, Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar and Home Minister Priyank Kharge had met the protesting students at the University of Agricultural Sciences in Gandhi Krishi Vignana Kendra. The Chief Minister assured them that the matter would be looked into and an appropriate decision would be taken. However, the students continued their protest and sat at Freedom Park, opposing the examination.
On Friday, Mr. Kharge visited the Freedom Park. Later, taking to social media, Mr. Kharge announced that a special committee of experts would be constituted to submit its report on the AO and AAO exam within 15 days. Based on the report, the necessary changes to the cadre and recruitment rules would be made.
“The agricultural officers’ recruitment examination scheduled for August 8 and 9 has been temporarily postponed. After the committee submits its report and it is examined, a new examination date will be announced at the earliest,” he said.
Published - August 06, 2026 11:20 pm IST

stories.headline: Karnataka High Court asks State’s response to plea complaining about impact of tunnel road project to Hebbal lake
stories.deck: Court warns authorities of staying the project if they failed to respond by August 24
stories.bodyText:
The High Court of Karnataka on Thursday ordered issue of notice to State government on a PIL petition questioning the project that envisages constructing a 2.2 km long three-lane, short transitory twin tunnel from Hebbal junction to the Karnataka Veterinary, Animal and Fisheries University (KVAFSU) at an estimated cost of ₹1,130 crore.
Also, the Court orally warned of staying the project if the Government and its authorities failed to file its response to the issues raised in the petition in writing before the next date of hearing on August 24.
A division bench comprising Chief Justice Vibhu Bakhru and Justice K.S. Hemalekha passed the order on the petition filed by Guruprasad R.K, a technocrat, Rishvanjas Raghavan, founder of Bengaluru Nava Nirmana Party’s youth wing, and Elizabeth Soumya, founder of Hebbal Nature Society.
Any study conducted?
Apart from responding to the issues raised in the petitions, the Bench directed the Government to file affidavit specifying if any study has been conducted on the impact of the project on Hebbal lake, and stating that whether studies have covered the question whether tunnel would cause any obstruction to lake’s inflow or outflow of water. The Bench also ordered issue of notice to M/s Rithwik Projects Pvt. Ltd., the contractor of the tunnel road project.
Contending that the project poses a severe threat to the ecologically sensitive Hebbal lake and has been approved by violating various provisions of the law, it has been pointed out in the petition that the Detailed Project Report (DPR) itself acknowledges the hydrological sensitivity of the area, noting groundwater movement and the need for a watertight structure near the lake.
Stating that the DPR admits that the tunnel will be just 8-12 metres from the lake boundary, the petition contends that this distance from the lake violates even the reduced buffer zones under the amended provisions of the Karnataka Tank Conservation and Development Authority Act.
Constitutional validity
Also, the petitioners have challenged the constitutional validity of the Karnataka Tank Conservation and Development Authority (Amendment) Act, 2025, which drastically reduced buffer zones around lakes.
The amendment replaced a uniform 30-metre buffer with a graded system based on a lake’s size, allowing for buffers as small as 0 to 1 metre for smaller lakes and reducing the buffer to 30 metres only for lakes over 100 acres, the Court said while contending reduction in buffer zone is scientifically unsound and a deliberate attempt to facilitate the tunnel project. Karnataka High Court asks State’s response to plea complaining about impact of tunnel road project to Hebbal lake.
The litigation also challenges Rule 24 of the Bengaluru Metropolitan Land Transport Authority (BMLTA) Rules, 2026. The petition terms amended rule a ‘colourable exercise” that attempts to retrospectively validate projects, including the Hebbal tunnel, initiated without the mandatory prior approval from the BMLTA.
Impact assessment
The petitioners have also sought a direction to restrain the authorities from proceeding with the project until comprehensive and independent hydrological, hydrogeological, groundwater, stormwater, flood-risk and cumulative environmental impact assessments are conducted by competent expert agencies and disclosed publicly, while seeking direction for constituting an independent panel of experts to assess impact on Hebbal lake, groundwater recharge, drainage, flood resilience and mobility.
Published - August 07, 2026 12:49 am IST

stories.headline: International Gay Games medallists from Karnataka urge the State to create inclusive sporting spaces
stories.deck: Goaty and Pawar were two of the three from India to participate in the International Gay Games 2026. The Gay Games is the world’s largest international LGBTQIA+ sporting and cultural event, held once every four years
stories.bodyText:
Highlighting that there are no avenues in India for people from the queer community to compete in sports, Goaty and Sumit Pawar, winners at the International Gay Games 2026, which recently concluded in Valencia, Spain, appealed to the State government to take proactive steps to make provisions for queer participation in sports.
“As a country, we are recognising three genders. But most of the sports spaces recognise only two. Other progressive countries have started adding non-binary as a category. India might need more time to add non-binary as a category, but at least if we can add third gender as a category, that will bring more inclusivity and offer everyone a space to participate,” said the athletes, speaking at a felicitation event held by the LGBTQIA+ and sports domains of the All India Professionals’ Congress.
Once in four years
Goaty and Pawar were two of the three Indians to participate in the International Gay Games 2026. The Gay Games is the world’s largest international LGBTQIA+ sporting and cultural event, held once every four years.
Goaty won four gold medals (High Jump, 5K Run, 10,000m Indoor Run, and Marathon in the Women’s 25–29 category), two silver medals (10K Run in the women’s 25–29 category and the overall women’s marathon), and a silver medal as part of the Mixed 4×400m Relay team. Sumit Pawar won the gold medal in Javelin Throw.
Originally hailing from Coimbatore and Rajasthan, respectively, both now call Bengaluru home and are members of the Bengaluru Front Runners (BRF), a community for LGBTQIA+ runners & walkers in the city.
Finding the connect
“I’ve been an athlete since I was very young, not the one who wins a lot, but the one who always participates,” said Goaty, who is an IGCSE teacher. After moving to Bengaluru, she joined the BRF.
While she was keen to participate in the previous Gay Games held in Hong Kong and Mexico in 2022, finances were an issue. Participation in Valencia Gay Games was realised with help from International Front Runners and Gay Games Federation.
“For me, running changed how I feel inside my body. Many of us might be able to relate to how disconnected we feel from our body as queer people. For me, running helped achieve that connect. Plus, there is the discipline that any kind of sport brings to our life,” Goaty said.
Goaty who started with 5km run, is now doing ultra marathons.
Above all, an athlete
“One of the best moments of my life was when, during the opening ceremony, we unfolded the Indian flag and entered the stadium. For me, in that moment, I wasn’t just someone from the queer community, but an athlete who’s representing India at the global stadium,” Pawar, who currenly works at Museum of Arts and Photography (MAP), beams with pride as he speaks.
The victory, however, doesn’t stop him or Goaty from challenging the status quo in Indian sports, where many disciplines receive far less attention and support than they deserve.
Pawar also points to the case of Dutee Chand, the first Indian athlete to come out as a member of the LGBTQIA+ community, who received backlash for the same.
“Why can’t an athlete be simply considered an athlete above anything else!” he wonders.
Pointing out that among the 10,000-odd participants at the Gay Games, only three were Indians. Goaty and Pawar hope that their participation paves the way for greater institutional and societal support and encourages more athletes from the queer community in India to take part in future editions.
Published - August 06, 2026 11:02 pm IST

stories.headline: 35 encroachments cleared on Bengaluru’s Vijayanagar Food Street
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru West City Corporation (BWCC) Thursday cleared 35 encroachments along a 250-metre stretch on both sides of Vijayanagar 6th Main Road. Popularly known as Vijayanagar Food Street, the road falls under Govindarajanagar division. The action followed a complaint before Lokayukta over illegal occupation of footpaths and inconvenience caused to motorists and pedestrians.
According to BWCC officials, food vendors would occupy one side of the stretch during evenings, while the opposite side had more permanent structures encroaching upon the footpath. Residents had complained that customers parked vehicles haphazardly along the road, leading to traffic congestion and obstructing pedestrian movement.
““For nearly 10 years, residents had been struggling with problems caused by the food street. The Lokayukta’s intervention has finally brought relief, and we hope the footpaths remain free of encroachments,” said Veeresh Bellur, a resident.
2.5k tonnes of debris cleared in 5 days
Bengaluru North City Corporation has scientifically disposed of 2,495 metric tonnes of construction and demolition (C&D) waste in the first five days of ‘Freedom from Waste’ campaign, officials said Thursday.
As part of the drive, commissioner Pommala Sunil Kumar conducted a surprise inspection of Marenahalli debris disposal site, one of the key facilities handling C&D waste. He reviewed debris disposal operations, vehicle movement, unloading processes and the site’s overall capacity to handle increasing volumes of waste.

stories.headline: Bengaluru may get 3 new botanical parks
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru
: Chief minister DK Shivakumar Wednesday said the state govt is exploring development of three large parks like Lalbagh and Cubbon Park in Bengaluru by utilising land owned by defence and forest departments, in a bid to expand green spaces for residents.
Speaking at the inauguration of Independence Day flower show at Lalbagh, Shivakumar said the city and its people require more green lung spaces and recreational spaces as its population continues to grow and urbanisation intensifies.
He said he has already identified three locations. “I will soon be meeting the defence minister 
Rajnath Singh
 and give my proposal to have a botanical park like Lalbagh in the defence land. I have already identified the location,” said Shivakumar. The proposed parks, he said, would remain under the ownership of the respective departments while being developed and maintained as public green spaces on the lines of Cubbon Park and Lalbagh.
Shivakumar said he has also held preliminary discussions with forest department and has asked various agencies, including GBA, BDA and horticulture department. “We are planning to create three to four parks during my tenure itself,” he said, adding a detailed meeting would be convened shortly to finalise the implementation strategy, responsibilities of each agency and framework for developing the parks.
Referring to a similar initiative in Varanasi, Shivakumar noted Varanasi municipal corporation had approved the exchange of more than 57 hectares of land with defence estate and railways to facilitate public amenities, including the creation of a 30-acre park. He said Bengaluru could adopt a similar model to unlock underutilised govt land for public benefit.

stories.headline: PM Surya Ghar sees more than tripling of daily rooftop solar installations in 9 months: MNRE Minister Pralhad Joshi
stories.deck: PM Surya Ghar has also crossed more than 50 lakh beneficiaries.
stories.bodyText:
India’s flagship PM Surya Ghar scheme has seen daily rooftop solar installations surge more than three-fold in the past nine months, Union Minister for New and Renewable Energy Pralhad Joshi said at the seventh CII International Energy Conference on Thursday.
“The pace of [daily] installations has increased about 3.2 times in just nine months from 5,000 installations per day in October 2025 to over 16,328 per day in July 2026,” he said.
Separately in his address, the Union Minister also stated that India has added non-fossil capacity of more than 300 gigawatts (GW) a decade ago and is “on path to cross 500 GW capacity by 2030”.
Mr. Joshi also reiterated that the PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana has more than 50 lakh beneficiaries with one lakh beneficiaries added every six days.
The flagship scheme seeks to provide free electricity to households by facilitating the installation of rooftop solar panels. The scheme closes on March 31, 2027.
Mr. Joshi also reiterated that the PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana has more than 50 lakh beneficiaries with one lakh beneficiaries added every six days. He also informed that about 19 lakh households are receiving zero electricity bills because of the scheme.
Further, more than 12 lakh households have cumulatively earned ₹421 crore through the sale of surplus power in fiscal year 2024-25., translating as an extra income of around ₹3,500 per year per household .
Published - August 06, 2026 10:22 pm IST

stories.headline: LIC Q1 net up 23% to ₹13,492 cr on higher premium and new biz
stories.deck: “Overall market share by first year premium income was 60.10% and this fits in well with our market share strategy”
stories.bodyText:
Life Insurance Corporation of India’s (LIC’s) standalone net profit for the June quarter rose 22.81% year-on-year (YoY) to ₹13,492 crore on higher premium income and a surge in value of new business (VNB).
Total premium income of the State-owned insurer increased 6.75% YoY to ₹1,27,250 crore. CEO and MD R.Doraiswamy said despite increasing competition in the life insurance industry, LIC was able to maintain its leadership in both individual and group business during the quarter.
“Our overall market share by first year premium income was 60.10% and this fits in well with our market share strategy. VNB has grown by 61% plus to ₹3,136 crore and VNB margin expanded by 7.5% to 22.90%. This is a direct outcome of our product diversification and distribution strategy,” he said.
Solvency ratio increased to 2.42% (2.17%). Assets Under Management (AUM) went up 4.10% YoY to ₹59,39,384 crore. Overall expense ratio increased by 16 bps (basis points) to 10.63%, LIC said in a release.
The insurer’s market share was 38.89% in individual business and 70.90% in the group business during the quarter. It sold 31,02,281 policies in the individual segment, showing an increase of 2.06% YoY.
The yield on investments on policyholder’s fund excluding unrealised gains was 8.28% (8.45%).
Mr..Doraiswamy said LIC will be completing 70 years of existence on September 1, 2026 and to mark the occasion, innovative product launches and other initiatives are planned.
On West Asia crisis impact on the life insurance business and whether it will continue, he said though the performance numbers have improved, the growth in premium or the APE (annual premium equivalent) is not “what you would have expected. Certainly we see, there can be some impacts, particularly the lines of business directly related to interest rates or the markets like ULIPS or annuity. We will have to wait and watch.”
On the recently concluded offer for sale, through which the government offloaded 6.5% stake in LIC; Mr. .Doraiswamy said it helped achieve the Securities and Exchange Board of India mandate of 10% minimum public shareholding ahead of the May 2027 deadline. With its stake reduced to 90%, the government does not have any immediate pressure to offload anything further.
On the 2032 deadline for the Centre to bring down its stake to 75% or in other words the MPS (minimum public shareholding) to be increased to 25%, he said “I don’t expect the government to come up with any new offers [for sale] in immediate future. The government has got time... five years is too long a period for them to work out,” he said.
Published - August 06, 2026 09:55 pm IST

stories.headline: India has coal stocks to meet 62 days of power demand: Coal Ministry
stories.deck: Coal production in July rose 7.51% on a year-over-year basis with dispatches growing 17.34%.
stories.bodyText:
India has adequate coal stocks to meet approximately 62 days of the domestic power sector’s consumption requirements, the Union Coal Ministry informed Thursday.
As of August 4, thermal power plants have about 34.55 million tonnes (MT) of coal, the ministry said, adding further, about 113 MT of coal was lying at pitheads and in-transit combined. Cumulatively, the total available stock stood at 148 MT.
“This is adequate to meet about 62 days of the power sector’s coal consumption requirement, providing a comfortable buffer,” the ministry emphasised.
Coal stocks indicated are specific to a period. With production ongoing, the stocks are replenished.
Overall coal production in July increased 7.51% year-on-year (YoY) to 69.75 MT. Dispatches during the reported period rose 17.34% YoY to 86.33 MT, according to provisional government data.
On a year-to-date basis until July in the current fiscal year, coal dispatches registered a growth of 5.87% YoY.
Published - August 06, 2026 06:42 pm IST

stories.headline: Lumina Datamatics acquires 100% stake of TNQTech
stories.bodyText:
Lumina Datamatics which is into content, retail support, and technology solutions, said it had acquired 100% stake in TNQTech, a Chennai-based publishing technology company and turned it it’s 100% subsidiary.
“This transaction marks a significant milestone in Lumina Datamatics’ organic and inorganic growth strategy and positions the combined organization among the world’s largest providers of scholarly publishing solutions,” the company said.
In December 2024, the company had signed a definitive agreement to acquire an 80% controlling stake in TNQTech.
“With the acquisition of the remaining 20%, the transaction has now been completed, making TNQTech a 100% wholly owned subsidiary of Lumina Datamatics,” the company said in a statement.
Sameer Kanodia, Vice Chairman and CEO, Lumina Datamatics & TNQTech, said, “The successful acquisition of TNQTech marks a defining milestone in our journey. Together, we have created a leading global partner for scholarly publishing solutions, combining deep domain expertise with next-generation AI technologies to help publishers transform their businesses.”
“Our focus is on driving the next wave of growth through innovation, AI-led transformation, and strategic investments in technology,” he added.
Mariam Ram, Founder and Director, TNQTech, said, “Becoming a part of Lumina Datamatics is the right step for TNQTech. Our technology and domain expertise align perfectly with their scale and reach in scholarly publishing.”
“I am confident TNQTech’s people, products and customers are now in the hands of a reliable, trusted organization that will carry our vision forward while driving the next phase of innovation and growth,” she stated.
The combined organisation will support publishers across the entire content lifecycle—from manuscript submission, peer review, and editorial workflows to production, digital publishing, accessibility, analytics, and AI-powered content enrichment.
Published - August 06, 2026 09:12 pm IST

stories.headline: Union Cabinet approves ₹23,371 crore GOBARdhan scheme to fuel CBG sector growth
stories.deck: The scheme aspires to increase domestic production of CBG ten-fold and mobilise large-scale private investment.
stories.bodyText:
The Union cabinet on Thursday approved the National Circular Bioenergy Scheme – GOBARdhan, provisioning a ₹23,731-crore as part of efforts to catalyse the growth of compressed biogas (CBG).
The GOBARdhan (Galvanising Organic Bio-Agro Resources Dhan) outlay, to be in place until 2036, seeks to increase domestic compressed biogas production nearly ten-fold through assured offtake, administered pricing, capital subsidies, pipeline infrastructure and easier access to finance, the government said.
The government emphasised the scheme would seek to impart a “strong and predictable framework” to fuel the uptick of the CBG ecosystem.
The programme would involve the use of agricultural residue, cattle dung, sugar industry waste such as press mud, municipal organic waste and other biomass to produce compressed biogas, which can be blended into CNG used in automobiles and also piped natural gas (PNG).
Welcoming the government initiative, A.R. Shukla, President of the Indian Biogas Association said the scheme addresses three imperatives -- remunerative price, assured offtake and capital support -- sought by the industry.
“This scheme delivers all three,” he said, adding, “moving from roughly 300 operating plants towards 5,000 [plants] will create lakhs of rural jobs. Industry must now respond with speed, quality and discipline. We commit our members to that. Waste-to-wealth is no longer a slogan; it is an investable business.”
Supporting pipeline infra
One of the most critical components is the development of the necessary pipeline infrastructure, which is essential for the widespread adoption of CBG, as it ensures reliable offtake and enables seamless integration with the broader gas grid.
GOBARdhan seeks to support both cluster-based and standalone pipeline infrastructure connecting CBG plants with trunk pipelines and city-gas distribution networks.
“Greater pipeline connectivity will reduce evacuation costs, improve reliability, expand market reach and enable higher utilization of domestically produced CBG,” said the government statement.
Imparting predictability
GOBARdhan further introduces a stable-administered price of ₹2,110 per Metric Million British Thermal Unit (MMBTU) for CBG.
The objective is to impart long-term revenue visibility alongside protecting consumer affordability. The scheme seeks to achieve this via a combination of government-centred support and a market-based cost-sharing mechanism.
Further, the scheme shall accord eligible greenfield and brownfield CBG projects looking to expand, with capital assistance of up to ₹2 crore per tonne per day (TPD) of installed CBG capacity.
Extending support across the spectrum, from core plant machinery to feedstock aggregation and manure processing, the scheme intends to lower the initial capital burden, speed up financial closure and increase participation from private entities, micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) and rural entrepreneurs.
The programme is expected to spur private investment, create additional income opportunities for farmers and rural entrepreneurs, improve management of agricultural and municipal waste, expand production of organic manure and lower greenhouse gas emissions.I
“Building on the progress already achieved, GOBARdhan will take India’s CBG journey from a strong foundation to a nationally scaled clean energy industry. It reflects the Government’s commitment to energy security, farmers and rural enterprises, waste-to-wealth, Atmanirbhar Bharat and the vision of Viksit Bharat.”

stories.headline: Real Madrid seals 7-year deal for Ivory Coast World Cup standout Yan Diomande
stories.deck: Diomande had an outstanding World Cup, and some Premier League teams were reportedly interested in signing him
stories.bodyText:
Real Madrid has reached a deal with Leipzig for the transfer of young Ivory Coast international Yan Diomande.
The Spanish powerhouse said on Thursday (August 6, 2026) that the 19-year-old forward will be linked to the club for the next seven seasons.
Diomande had an outstanding World Cup, and some Premier League teams were reportedly interested in signing him. Leipzig had been saying he was not for sale.
Ivory Coast was eliminated by Norway in the World Cup round of 32.
Leipzig sporting director Marcel Schäfer said Diomande “impressed us with his carefree attitude, willingness to learn, and courage from day one.”
“He quickly established himself at the highest level with us, showcasing his speed, dribbling skills, and goal-scoring threat.”
He said the club was proud that Diomande's performances “garnered significant international attention.”
Paris Saint-Germain also was reportedly interested in signing the young forward.
It was not yet clear if Diomande would initially be registered with Madrid's B squad.
Madrid's main team has been revamped since a disappointing end to last season. The new signings who will be coached by José Mourinho include playmaker Bernardo Silva, centre back Ibrahima Konaté, right back Denzel Dumfries and left back Marc Cucurella.
Published - August 07, 2026 02:26 am IST

stories.headline: Uruguay appoint Forlan as head coach after World Cup debacle
stories.deck: The 47-year-old former Manchester ​United, Atletico Madrid and Inter ⁠Milan forward succeeds Marcelo Bielsa, who left after a winless group-stage exit in Uruguay's ‌World Cup campaign
stories.bodyText:
Diego Forlan has been named head coach of Uruguay's senior and Under-20s sides, the country's FA (AUF) announced on Thursday (August 6, 2026).
The 47-year-old former Manchester United, Atletico Madrid and Inter Milan forward succeeds Marcelo Bielsa, who left after a winless group-stage exit in Uruguay's World Cup campaign.
Forlan will begin his tenure immediately with the Under-20 team, the AUF said.
"Forlan returns to where he left an indelible mark," the AUF said in a statement.
"A role model, icon, and emblem of an unforgettable generation, the best player of the 2010 South Africa World Cup returns now to contribute his experience, leadership, and profound knowledge of international football from a technical position."
The appointment is part of Uruguay's efforts to rebuild following Bielsa's departure.
The Argentine left when his contract expired and acknowledged in a press conference that he had been unable to mould a talented squad into one capable of avoiding disappointment at the World Cup.
Local media reports also highlighted tensions between Bielsa and some members of the squad during the tournament.
Forlan, who won 112 caps and helped Uruguay lift the 2011 Copa America title, retired from playing in 2019 and has since coached Uruguayan clubs Penarol and Atenas.
He will take charge of Uruguay's friendly matches scheduled between September and November.
Published - August 07, 2026 02:13 am IST

stories.headline: Jos Buttler backs Vaibhav Sooryavanshi to break his all-time T20 runs record
stories.deck: It's really cool, actually, to think you've got the most T20 runs out of anyone. Someone will surpass it one day - and his name's probably [Vaibhav] Sooryavanshi - but it's a proud moment, Buttler said
stories.bodyText:
England star Jos Buttler, who surpassed West Indies legend Kieron Pollard to become the leading run-getter in T20 history on Wednesday (August 5, 2026), backed the teen Indian batting sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi to surpass the record one day.
Buttler climbed the summit of T20 cricket during his side Manchester Super Giants (MSG) match against Welsh Fire in the Men's Hundred, scoring a quickfire 51* in 20 balls, with two fours and six sixes at a strike rate of 250.00.
In 522 T20s, Buttler has now scored 14,833 runs with nine centuries and 105 fifties, outdoing Pollard (14,803 runs in 746 matches with two centuries) and a long-time record-holding West Indies titan Chris Gayle (14,562 runs in 463 matches with 22 centuries and 88 fifties).
After setting the record, Buttler, as per Cricinfo quoting Sky Sports, said he was proud to become the highest run-scorer in T20 cricket but said that the record would eventually be broken, adding that the likely person to surpass it could be Vaibhav Sooryavanshi.
"It's really cool, actually, to think you've got the most T20 runs out of anyone. Someone will surpass it one day - and his name's probably [Vaibhav] Sooryavanshi - but it's a proud moment," Buttler told Sky Sports as per Cricinfo.
At just 15, Sooryavanshi enjoyed a remarkable run in T20I cricket, scoring 151 runs in three matches against Zimbabwe to claim his maiden Player of the Series award as India completed a 3-0 clean sweep.
His success came on the back of a stellar ICC Men's Under-19 Cricket World Cup campaign earlier this year, where he amassed 439 runs and was named Player of the Tournament, further highlighting his immense potential.
Buttler said he would have liked to overtake Pollard while playing against MI London with Pollard watching as the head coach, and expressed pride at joining a list of T20 greats.
"We played against MI London last game and it would have been nice to get past Polly while he was there sat in the dugout, but there's some great names on there, some special players, so I'm really proud of that," Buttler said.
Coming to the Men's Hundred match, Welsh Fire elected to bat first at Manchester.
Knocks from Matt Short (71 in 47 balls, with eight fours and two sixes) and Phil Salt (48 in 37 balls, with three fours and three sixes) steered them to 155/4 in 100 balls.
During the chase, MSG came out all guns blazing, with Tim Seifert (62* in 36 balls, with 10 fours), Paul Walter (37 in 18 balls, with four boundaries) and Buttler (51* in 20 balls, with two fours and six sixes) chasing the total with nine wickets to spare.
Published - August 07, 2026 01:42 am IST

stories.headline: CSA include 3 T20Is to India women's tour of South Africa
stories.deck: The Indian team will spend an extra week in South Africa to play the T20I series between December 26 and 30
stories.bodyText:
The Cricket South Africa on Thursday (August 6, 2026) revised the schedule of India women’s team tour later this year to accommodate three T20Is in addition to a Test and three ODIs.
As per the revised itinerary, the one-off Test will be played from December 9-12 before the ODI series kicks in from December 16-22.
Now, the Indian team will spend an extra week in South Africa to play the T20I series between December 26 and 30.
The T20Is will be played at Benoni and Potchefstroom, which the CSA felt will give both the sides a good platform going into the inaugural Women's Champions Trophy, which will be played in Sri Lanka in February.
“We are delighted to confirm the revised schedule for India's tour of South Africa, with the addition of the T20 International series over the festive period, ensuring our Proteas Women have the best possible preparation ahead of the inaugural ICC Women's Champions Trophy in Sri Lanka early next year,” Pholetsi Moseki, the CSA CEO, said in a statement.
“India remain one of the strongest teams in world cricket, and the opportunity to compete against them across all three formats will provide invaluable competition as we continue building towards another major ICC event,” said Moseki.
India had toured South Africa in March-April this year for a T20I series which they lost 1-4.
The two teams then clashed in the T20 World Cup in England, where SA beat India to dent their chances of entering the semifinal.
Published - August 07, 2026 01:37 am IST

stories.headline: Three Indians make finals of World Athletics U20 Championships
stories.deck: Yadav topped the men's javelin Group A qualification round with a throw of 69.87m and ended at second spot overall, behind South Africa's title favourite Jan-Hendrik Heymans who won Group B with a 76.02m throw
stories.bodyText:
Javelin throwers Ashish Yadav and T Dharanidharan along with discus thrower Amanat Kamboj qualified for the final rounds in a decent opening day performance by the Indians at the World Athletics U20 Championships in the U.S.
Yadav topped the men's javelin Group A qualification round with a throw of 69.87m and ended at second spot overall, behind South Africa's title favourite Jan-Hendrik Heymans who won Group B with a 76.02m throw. The 19-year-old Indian has a season's best of 74.49m, which is also his personal best.
Heymans was the lone competitor to breach the automatic qualification mark of 72.50m.
Dharanidharan made it to the final round, taking the 12th and the last spot overall after finishing fifth in Group B qualification round with a throw of 68.07m.
Those who breached the automatic qualifying mark of 72.50m or at least best 12 qualified for the final to be held on Friday.
Indian superstar Neeraj Chopra is the current world record holder in the event with his 86.48m throw in the 2016 edition of the championships in Bydgoszcz, Poland.
In women's discus throw, Amanat produced a season's best throw of 52.58m to finish sixth in Group A qualification round and take the 12th and last available spot to sneak into the finals.
China's Su Yixin took the top position across the two qualification groups with 58.06m, while compatriot Ma Chenyi was second with 57.72m.
Those who breached the automatic qualifying mark of 55m or the best 12 performers qualified for the final to be held later tonight.
Mogali Venkatram made it to the men's 800m semifinals while Uwin Anand bowed out of the same event after the Round 1 heat races.
Venkatram finished third in Heat 5, clocking 1 minute 52.81 seconds to secure his place in the semifinals. Anand ended seventh in Heat 1 and 30th overall, clocking 1:52.37sec.
Across the five heats, Uganda's Shafeck Murungi recorded the fastest time, clocking a personal best of 1:46.64sec.
First five in each heat plus two fastest runners from the remaining athletes across the five heats qualify for the semifinal.
The Indian 4×400m mixed relay team exited the competition in the Round 1 itself after finishing fourth in its heat with a time of 3 minute 22.85 seconds.
The quartet of Piyush Raj, Tahura Khatun, Sayed Sabeer and Thiya Arumugam finished 11th overall across three heats.
USA topped Round 1 with a time of 3:18.26. The top three teams from each of the three heats advance to the final.
In the 2022 edition of the biennial championships, India had claimed a historic silver medal in the mixed 4x400m relay with an Asian U20 record time of 3:17.76sec, which is still the second best time in the world U20 records.
Published - August 07, 2026 01:12 am IST
